# PhysxVehicleAPI

Makes a rigid body the chassis of a [PhysX](glossary.md#physx) vehicle whose wheels are the descendants with PhysxVehicleWheelAttachmentAPI. Listing it turns on vehicle parsing for the attach; the walkers enumerate the prims that list it, and the runtime then resolves the drive, checks which other vehicle APIs the [prim](glossary.md#prim) lists, and validates and creates the vehicle.

- **Applies to:** [`Xformable`](glossary.md#xformable)
- **Requires on the same prim:** [`PhysicsRigidBodyAPI`](PhysicsRigidBodyAPI.md)
- **Read only when listed in [`usd-schemas`](prim.md#columns).**
- **No builder:** `ovphysx.population` and `Population.hpp` do not write this component; the consumer reads it when another population writes it.

## Columns

*Raw fallback* is the [USD](glossary.md#usd) schema value. *Producer writes* is what [ovstage](glossary.md#ovstage) population puts in the column for a USD stage. *Parser default* applies on the consumer when the column is absent, in stage units. **diverges** means writing the raw fallback literally parses differently from omitting the column (the parser default): USD population may well publish that very value for an unauthored attribute, so the marker is about the column being present, not about its value.

| Column | Type | Units | Raw fallback | Producer writes | Parser default | If absent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `physxVehicle:drive` | uint64 array, RELATIONSHIP_PATH_ID |  |  | not written |  | No drive from the relationship: a PhysxVehicleDriveStandardAPI or PhysxVehicleDriveBasicAPI on the vehicle prim itself is the drive (both listed logs an error and the vehicle is not created); with neither the vehicle has no drive, and PhysxVehicleWheelControllerAPI on its wheel attachments is the only torque input. |
| `usd-metadata:customData:physxVehicle:referenceFrameIsCenterOfMass` | bool8 |  |  | the nested customData physxVehicle -> referenceFrameIsCenterOfMass value | true | The legacy vehicle frame is the center-of-mass frame. |

## Interactions

- **[`PhysicsRigidBodyAPI`](PhysicsRigidBodyAPI.md):** Required on the same prim, which must also be Xformable; otherwise the runtime logs an error and the vehicle is not created. physics:rigidBodyEnabled false, or physics:kinematicEnabled true while physxVehicle:vehicleEnabled is true, also invalidates the vehicle.

## Notes

- The runtime checks whether the vehicle prim lists PhysxVehicleMultiWheelDifferentialAPI, PhysxVehicleTankDifferentialAPI, PhysxVehicleSteeringAPI, PhysxVehicleAckermannSteeringAPI or PhysxVehicleBrakesAPI; when one is listed but its parser rejected the data, the vehicle is not created. Each of them, and PhysxVehicleControllerAPI, needs the vehicle to have a drive.
- The runtime also reads physxVehicle:vehicleEnabled, limitSuspensionExpansionVelocity, subStepThresholdLongitudinalSpeed, lowForwardSpeedSubStepCount, highForwardSpeedSubStepCount, the four slip-denominator attributes, the sticky-tire speed, time and damping attributes, physxVehicle:suspensionLineQueryType and the customData flag physxVehicle:referenceFrameIsCenterOfMass. Live changes are applied to vehicleEnabled, limitSuspensionExpansionVelocity, the sticky-tire attributes and every slip denominator except the deprecated minLongitudinalSlipDenominator. They are not described yet.
- At load the runtime fills the lateral sticky-tire threshold time from physxVehicle:longitudinalStickyTireThresholdTime (a historical schema mismatch), so physxVehicle:lateralStickyTireThresholdTime is not read at load and only takes effect as a live change.
